purpose: R251 non-financial HS300 capex-intensity improvement factor versus a matched quality-cash control

universe.industry_source: current ext_hy_ths industry snapshot; not historical PIT

factor.formula: capex_intensity_improvement_yoy = capex_t_minus_1 / revenue_t_minus_1 - capex_t / revenue_t; positive means lower capital intensity than the prior annual report
factor.pit_rule: annual reports only; effective date = max(vendor notice_date + 1 calendar day, statutory reporting deadline + 3 calendar days); values expire after 500 calendar days

pit_audit.rule: annual capex and revenue; effective date = max(vendor notice_date + 1 calendar day, statutory reporting deadline + 3 calendar days); latest annual report expires after 500 calendar days

samples.rolling_1y: 252-trading-day rolling compounded return over the stitched 2023-2026 curve
samples.recent_12m: last 252 trading-day returns of the stitched 2023-2026 curve

execution.cost_stress: 4x and 5x scale all four components proportionally
execution.stitching: two segment returns compounded into one curve; first day of each later segment skipped

caveats: Annual reports update only once per year, so the signal can become stale within the fiscal year.
Capex classifications can mix maintenance and expansion spending with different economic meaning.
The discovery segment starts in 2023 because two consecutive annual reports are required.
Large declines from a high prior-year intensity base can dominate the cross-section.
Financial values are current snapshots and may contain restatements.
The industry snapshot used to exclude financials is current rather than historical PIT.
The full curve is stitched from two system-engine segments; segment boundaries can reset an open position.
Trade P&L shares are contribution diagnostics from two segments each starting at 1,000,000 notional, not a compounded-return decomposition.
The factor is research-only until every preregistered gate passes; passing would justify paper-trading validation, not production deployment.
